artboards.title: Alt B — no cage, polished collar

annotations.text:
Goalhorn — main screen redesign

Same screen, same tokens as the app today (dark radial room, #8A8A90 idle label, #FF4D3D GOAL!, the 3-bar settings glyph, red tab tint). What changed is the light itself.

Tap the first artboard to fire it.

What makes it read as a real fixture

1. Squat, not tall. A rink light is wider than it is high. The old lamp was a tall narrow tube, which reads as a lantern.

2. The cage wraps. Bars sit at even angles around the cylinder, so on screen they bunch toward the silhouette and thin out (x = R·sin0, width = w0·cos0). Over the dome each bar follows its actual meridian, so it hugs the glass instead of bowing past it.

3. Hoops obey perspective. Above eye level the near half bulges up, below it sags down, their ends darken as they turn away, and the back halves show faintly through the glass curving the other way.

4. The cage stands proud of the glass and drops a soft offset shadow onto it.

5. Cylinder shading. A left-to-right falloff under the red is what turns a red shape into a glass tube. The rim also pipes light the way thick glass does.

6. The lamp sits LOW in the dome, so the hot spot is low and the cap stays deeper red.

7. Idle is OFF - deep near-black cherry glass, so the fired state actually hits.

8. The room reacts: two opposing beams off a spinning reflector, a pool of light on the surface, red bounce caught on the steel, and film grain over everything.

Two alternates for the glass/hardware — same room, same screen, so you are judging one variable.

Alt A — Fresnel beacon: horizontal lens ribs. Throws harder, more defined beams and looks more like emergency-vehicle hardware. Busier behind the cage.

Alt B — no cage: polished collar, bare dome, cleaner product-shot read. Loses the arena-hardware character that the cage gives it.

Main uses smooth glass + cage, which is closest to the real rink fixture.
